50/G.goal: Explain the end-to-end process for building and validating a realistic walking-behavior model to optimize system-controlled navigation in virtual reality.
50/G.achieves: It gives the learner a foundational optimization technique for VR experience design, enabling them to evaluate how natural movement modeling affects perceived realism, user preference, and the limits of realism alone in addressing cybersickness.

50/O1.goal: Explain how a realistic slow-in-slow-out walking-behavior model for system-controlled VR navigation is derived from empirical walking data, represented with Fourier-series motion and visual gain, and validated in users.
50/O1.achieves: It lets the learner understand a concrete optimization strategy for VR navigation by showing how natural walking dynamics can increase perceived realism and preference while still requiring separate cybersickness countermeasures.
